subject: Rate split exception & implementation window for GPU capacity
messages:
From: Megan Ortiz <megan@havenly.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, procurement@havenly.ai
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: additional GPU capacity + proposed price split

Hi Mina,

Quick note from procurement at HavenlyAI — we need to increase our committed GPU pool for inference starting July. Current committed vCPU/GPU footprint is 40 A100-equivalent units; we're asking to increase to 80 committed units, with a negotiated price split between committed and burst usage for the first 90 days of the ramp.

High-level ask:
- Add 40 committed GPU units to Exhibit A (Order Form) effective 2026-07-01.
- Apply a two-tier price ladder for the first 90 days: committed priced at the current committed rate, burst billed at a temporary discounted burst rate (we've proposed a 20% discount on burst for the ramp period).
- We need a documented rollback/rollback-cap plan in case we miss performance SLAs.

Attached: cost_proposal_q2_v2.xlsx (estimates) and a draft acceptance checklist.

Can Redwood prepare a change order / amendment draft and an implementation runbook with a go-live date of 2026-07-01? Procurement would like legal redlines and a final DocuSign-ready orderform by 2026-06-22.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Megan Ortiz
Head of Platform
HavenlyAI Inc
megan@havenly.ai

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan@havenly.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: additional GPU capacity + proposed price split

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment.

We can support the capacity uplift and the temporary price-split approach, but a few clarifying items before we start drafting:

1) Exhibit reference: can you confirm whether this sits under Exhibit A (Order Form) only or if you expect any MSA-level pricing language to be amended (e.g., a temporary rate-ladder in Section 3)?
2) Acceptance criteria: please attach the acceptance checklist you mentioned (I saw an outline but not a definitive set of signals). We need explicit success metrics for the 30/60/90 day checkpoints.
3) Rollback path: are you expecting an automatic rollback based on performance thresholds or a manual rollback triggered by ops?

Proposed internal owners & next steps:
- Sales (Karthik) to own drafting the amended Order Form and price ladder.
- Legal (Laura) to review MSA redlines if any (please see Laura on CC).
- Solutions/Delivery (me) to produce the implementation runbook and a canary rollout plan.

I attached an implementation template (capacity_runbook.xlsx) with fields we need filled by your ops team (forecast by day, expected burst traffic patterns, and SLO targets). If procurement can populate that by EOD Tue (2026-06-16) we'll aim to have a draft order form to legal the same day.

I'll tentatively schedule an internal sync tomorrow to align the draft.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Thanks Megan / Mina — looping in a few pricing notes so legal has context for redlines.

Background & proposal (sales view):
- We can honor the requested committed increase to 80 units. Commercially, we prefer to keep committed pricing unchanged and apply the temporary discount to burst only (as Megan suggested).
- Operationally, we recommend splitting billing so that committed units are billed against the committed SKU and burst usage is invoiced against a short-term ramp SKU ("ramp-burst-90d") so accounting can reconcile.

Exception path we need legal to confirm:
- Temporary rate ladder to be timebound to 90 days from go-live. After 90 days, native burst pricing applies automatically unless mutually amended. We need an explicit clause in the Order Form: "Temporary Ramp Pricing" with an effective start and end date and an automatic reversion clause.
- Canary rollout: 2-week canary targeting 10% of inference traffic, then 50% for week 3, full cutover by week 5. Acceptance gates at day 30/60/90.

Attached: draft_orderform_v2_redlines.pdf (sales-drafted tracked changes — draft pricing table and temporary SKU language).

Laura — can you review the attached and advise on the wording for the "automatic reversion" and whether we need any MSA-level language? If legal can return marked-up edits by EOD Thu (2026-06-18) we can meet procurement's 2026-06-22 DocuSign target.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Ortiz <megan@havenly.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: additional GPU capacity + proposed price split

Thanks — I reviewed the sales draft. High level: commercial structure is acceptable but legal needs a consolidated tracked-change Order Form and clear guidance on the following before we sign off:

1) "Automatic reversion" language: acceptable in principle but must include an explicit notice window (we recommend 30 days prior written notice before automatic reversion). We'll propose: "Temporary Ramp Pricing shall expire 90 days after the Effective Ramp Start Date unless the Parties execute a written amendment. Redwood will provide 30 days' prior written notice of reversion to standard rates."

2) Indemnity / liability carve-out: for ramped burst usage we need to ensure SLA credits are limited — propose a capped credit remedy for performance-impacting events during the ramp. Please advise expected cap (percentage of ramp fees) — sales, please propose a number.

3) Data residency & DPA: customer mentions expanded capacity which could touch private deployment regions. If the underlying capacity touches EU-hosted data, we need the DPA addendum. Megan — can you confirm if any EU data will be processed?

4) Change order format: please submit a single PDF with tracked changes (redlines) including Exhibit A and any MSA cross-references. I cannot reconcile piecemeal notes.

If the team consolidates and sends a single redlined Order Form and the populated capacity_runbook.xlsx by EOD Fri (2026-06-19), legal can deliver a marked-up DocuSign-ready draft by EOD Sun (2026-06-20). After that we can get signatures and circulate the DocuSign link.

For reference: HubSpot deal HVN-2026-06-001 is linked here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567. I've also populated a checklist in the shared folder.

Attaching: legal_quicknotes_ramp.docx (summary) and placeholder for DocuSign link: docusign_orderform_link.txt

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
